paper.title_en: Revisiting the cosmological model of Hubble parameter using f(Q) gravity
paper.abstract_en: In this study, we have revisited the isotropic and homogeneous cosmological model within the framework of f(Q) gravity, where Q denotes the non-metricity term. The solution of field equations are obtained by taking a time-dependent scale factor $a(t)= \big (\sinh (\alpha t)\big )^{\frac{1}{n}}$ and specific form of f(Q) gravity $f(Q)= Q + \eta Q^{\delta }$, where $\alpha $, n, $\eta $ and $\delta $ are arbitrary constants. We calculate all the parameters by using the estimated values obtained from observational Hubble dataset. We analyze various cosmic features of the derived model such as the deceleration parameter q, the energy density $\rho $, the pressure p, and the EoS parameter $\omega $. The physical viability of the model is also examined through the analysis of energy conditions. We also investigate the speed of sound and jerk parameter associated with the proposal model that indicates the stability of a dark energy model. Our findings provide deeper insights into the dynamics of dark energy and its role in the accelerated expansion of the universe.
